newsitem.title: USA: Millennium says patent claims allowed.
newsitem.headline: Millennium says patent claims allowed.

text.p: Millennium Pharmaceuticals Inc and Roche Holding Ltd's Hoffmann-La Roche Inc Friday said Millennium has received a notice of allowance from the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office for patent claims related to a human gene called Uncoupling Protein Homologue (UCPH), important in weight modulation.

Beginning in 1994, Millennium said it started filing a number of U.S. patent applications related to this gene and its use in therapeutic, diagnostic and drug screening applications related to weight modulation and thermogenesis, the production of heat.
Roche has an exclusive license under this family of patent applications in certain fields.

"Increasing the expression of this gene, or increasing the activity of the protein, should result in weight loss due to increased energy expenditure," noted Millennium scientist Louis Tartaglia, Ph.D. "The UCPH gene may explain why some people appear to have an easier time burning off excess calories. Increasing UCPH activity in obese people may allow their metabolism to assist in weight loss."
